title: Quiz 5 — magnetic supercells: multi-Q, conical and distorted spirals

questions.question: Which of these states can NOT be treated with the rotating frame and needs the supercell workflow?

options.b: a conical spiral in a field along the spiral axis
options.c: a DMI helix with D ∥ n

questions.explanation: The field adds a uniform component: the state is not a planar spiral, so the planar rotating-frame ansatz fails.

questions.question: Why does an easy axis lying in the spiral plane force a supercell?

options.b: it breaks invariance under rotations about n, so R_n^T A R_n ≠ A and the spiral distorts (harmonics)

questions.explanation: Only anisotropy along n keeps the Hamiltonian rotation invariant; in-plane anisotropy bunches the spins (3q, 5q harmonics).

questions.question: What does the Luttinger–Tisza (LT) scan return?

options.a: the exact ground state in every case
options.b: the q minimising the lowest eigenvalue of J(q): the ordering vector and a lower bound of the energy

questions.explanation: LT minimises the Fourier-transformed coupling matrix with the spin-length constraint relaxed: a lower bound, exact for simple cases.

questions.question: What is the 'star' of q_LT used for?

options.b: the set of symmetry-equivalent wave vectors that a multi-Q state can combine; all must fit the supercell

questions.explanation: Crystal rotations map q_LT to equivalent q's; triple-Q states use the three members of a hexagonal star.

questions.question: Why does SymPhase keep n × n supercells when the star has several members (triangular lattice)?

options.b: a strip n1 ≠ n2 cannot contain all three Q's at 120°, so no triple-Q (skyrmion) state could form

questions.explanation: Without equal sizes only one star member is commensurate; the multi-Q state is excluded by construction.

questions.question: Hands-on: the J1–J2 chain with J1 = −1, J2 = 0.5 meV: how many cells does the automatic supercell have? (chain()['M'])
questions.explanation: q = 1/6 exactly, so the 6-cell supercell has zero LT penalty.

questions.question: Hands-on: J2 = 0.4 (q_exact = 0.14255). Which supercell length n between 4 and 13 gives the lowest energy per cell?
questions.explanation: 1/7 = 0.1429 is the closest m/n to 0.14255 for n ≤ 13; the energy is not monotonic in n.

questions.question: Hands-on: energy per cell (meV) of the best J2 = 0.4 approximant (4 decimals)?
questions.explanation: −0.712498 meV, only 2 × 10⁻⁶ meV above the exact rotating-frame value −0.7125.

questions.question: Hands-on: cone angle: cos θ of the J1–J2 chain (S = 1, g = 2) in B = 2 T along z (3 decimals)?
Hands-on: for that cone, what is the uniform structure-factor weight w(0) (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: w(0) = cos²θ = 0.2144; the remaining 0.7856 sits at ±Q.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many zero (Goldstone) modes at Γ does the cone have in its supercell?
questions.explanation: Only rotations about the field direction remain a continuous symmetry.

questions.question: Hands-on: which harmonic appears for K = 0.4 meV along x in the 6-cell J1–J2 spiral?
questions.explanation: A uniaxial anisotropy ∝ cos²φ couples φ to 2φ, producing odd harmonics; 3q is the first (weight ≈ 0.015).

questions.question: Why does SymPhase relax from many seeds (LT single-Q, conical, multi-Q, random)?

options.b: the energy landscape has several local minima; the lowest of many starts is the ground-state candidate

questions.explanation: Different phases (cycloid, cone, skyrmion crystal, FM) are separate minima; reaching the lowest from several seeds is the check.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many skyrmions does the 10 × 10 triangular supercell contain at B = 14 T (|N_sk|)?
questions.explanation: N_sk = −3: the skyrmion-lattice cell is one third of the supercell, fixed by |Q|.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many members has the star of q_LT for the triangular skyrmion model (±q identified)?
questions.explanation: Three wave vectors at 120°: the triple-Q skyrmion crystal combines all of them.

questions.question: Hands-on: sequence of ground states of the skyrmion model with increasing field (10×10 cell)?
questions.explanation: 0–6 T: (distorted) cycloid; ≈ 8–20 T: skyrmion crystal (N_sk = −3); ≥ 24 T: ferromagnet.

questions.question: Hands-on: the magnetic space group of the skyrmion crystal (symphase tensors on supercell/POSCAR + INCAR)?
questions.explanation: Polar 6m'm': no T, no PT; a T-odd antisymmetric σ_xy (Hall response) is allowed.

questions.question: How is the lattice topological charge computed?

options.b: sum of solid angles Ω of the spin triangles of every lattice triangle, divided by 4π (Berg–Lüscher)

questions.explanation: Ω = 2 atan2(e1·(e2×e3), 1 + e1·e2 + e2·e3 + e3·e1); the sum is an integer for a smooth texture.

questions.question: A supercell of N primitive cells with one magnetic atom per cell gives how many magnon bands?

options.b: N (folded into the smaller supercell Brillouin zone)

questions.explanation: Bands are folded: N sites → N bosonic modes per k of the supercell zone.

questions.question: Which VASP setup checks a predicted non-collinear supercell texture?

options.a: vasp_std with ISPIN = 2 and collinear MAGMOM
options.b: vasp_ncl with LNONCOLLINEAR, MAGMOM from supercell/INCAR, constrained moments, LSORBIT if DMI matters

questions.explanation: Then compare total energies with competing states (seeds.dat) in the same supercell.
